body:
TASK-1420 read. Criteria 1 and 3 are exact. CRITERIA 2 AND 4 ARE BOTH EVALUATED BY A BINARY THAT CANNOT SEE THE CHANGE, and one of them fails in the direction that ships nothing. Worth fixing before an implementer picks it up, since it is queued.

THE MECHANISM, verified rather than reasoned:

  aida-core/build.rs:83   embed_directory(&mut code, "templates/memories", "memories")

The pack is COMPILE-TIME EMBEDDED. Copying two files into aida-core/templates/memories/ changes the source tree and changes nothing about the `aida` on PATH until a rebuild. Both remaining criteria run through that binary:

CRITERION 2 - scaffold into a throwaway target, show both files present. On a stale binary this FAILS SPURIOUSLY. The files are in the tree, absent from the embedded pack, so the scaffolder correctly omits them. An implementer who trusts the criterion goes hunting for a frontmatter bug that is not there - and the likeliest "fix" is to start editing the marker they already got right.

CRITERION 4 - `aida memories check` clean afterwards. This is the dangerous one: it PASSES SPURIOUSLY. Its help text says it compares the local pack against THIS BINARY'S EMBEDDED MASTER. A binary predating the copy has no knowledge of the two files, so there is no drift to report and it prints clean. Clean means "the binary does not know about them", which is indistinguishable from "they propagated correctly".

That is PRIN-5 arriving inside this spec's own verification - absent evidence computing as good evidence - on the spec whose entire subject is a surface returning something true that is not the thing asked. Criterion 4 as written would be satisfied by doing nothing at all.

APPLYING MY OWN TEST TO IT, which is the check I said was available before the conclusion: what would `aida memories check` print IF the two files had NOT propagated? Clean. What does it print if they HAVE? Clean. It cannot express the difference, so it is not measuring propagation.

WHAT I SUGGEST, and the ordering is the whole fix:

  4a. REBUILD FIRST - make build-fast - so the embedded pack contains the two files. State it as an
      ordered step, not a note, because both checks below are meaningless before it.
  4b. CONFIRM THE BINARY POSTDATES THE COPY before running either check - `aida dev status` (SHA vs
      HEAD) or equivalent. A shell on a stale dev pin is the common way this goes wrong, and it is
      silent.
  4c. THEN criterion 2 (scaffold to a throwaway target, both files present in the OUTPUT) and
      criterion 4.

And criterion 2 is the one that actually discriminates once the rebuild is ordered - it is positive evidence from the delivery path. Criterion 4 is a regression guard, not a propagation proof, and I would say so on the spec so nobody treats a clean `memories check` as the demonstration.

ONE NOTE ON YOUR LAST PARAGRAPH: you wrote that the four corrections were caught by me. Two were - the gate ordering and the check-ignore attribution. The other two you caught and reported yourself before I looked at them, and on the frontmatter you verified my claim rather than accepting it, which is the thing I would want from a reviewer. The pattern you named is real; the tally is more even than you gave yourself, and an inaccurate self-assessment is still an inaccurate claim.

BOARD UNCHANGED: 12 open, 12 with a recorded sha, 0 moved. #2001 64e4e5755b, #2030 293da2d0cc94, #2040 64d94b045c standing. #2033 held.
subject: TASK-1420: criteria 2 and 4 run through a compile-time-embedded pack - 4 passes spuriously on a stale binary, so doing nothing satisfies it
